author: Newsweek
title: FOX may earn $450M from World Cup hydration breaks: Report
text:
Newly implemented hydration breaks are an extremely divisive issue at the 2026 FIFA men's World Cup — and extremely profitable.
one hydration break 22 minutes into each half for this World Cup, regardless of if the match is in an air-conditioned dome or what the temperature is outdoors.
"This is a way to get an ad break in the first and an ad break in the second half," Skipper said on"On Wednesday, July 8, Sportico reported FOX's earnings from broadcasting this World Cup so far, and the numbers back up Skipper. "The hydration breaks alone will ensure that FOX will walk away from this year’s World Cup with a tidy profit — especially since the cost of entry was so low," Sportico'sreported.
"With approximately 260 additional seconds of ad time to sell per match, Fox booked nearly $200 million in bonus sales during the group stage alone, and is on pace to realize a total of some $450 million worth of glug-glug revenue when all is said and done.
" The final seven matches of this World Cup will demand peak viewership, too, with eight powerhouses remaining: Argentina, Belgium, England, France, Norway, Morocco, Spain, and Switzerland. France and Morocco's quarterfinal meeting on Thursday, July 9, is a much-anticipated rematch of the 2022 World Cup semifinal, which France won. Argentina and Lionel Messi are still alive and vying to become the first repeat men's World Cup champions since 1958 and 1962.
Norway and England will have stars littered all over the pitch on Saturday, July 11. The 2026 World Cup final is scheduled for Sunday, July 19, at MetLife Stadium. And while we don't yet know which teams will feature, we do know thatare BTS, Justin Bieber, Madonna, and Shakira, with Burna Boy, Gustavo Dudamel, the PS22 Chorus, and Coldplay also set to perform. Cash cow, indeed.
